questions: Do you remember what happened during this episode after you were fully awake?
Were you asleep immediately before the episode began?
Have you previously gotten out of bed or behaved unusually while still asleep?
Has anyone observed you sleepwalking, talking, or eating during sleep?
Did you seem confused or difficult to awaken during the episode?
Did you have rhythmic jerking, stiffening, or repeated movements of your arms or legs?
Did your eyes remain open, deviate to one side, or stare blankly?
Did you bite your tongue or lose bladder or bowel control?
Were you confused, unusually sleepy, or had a severe headache after the episode?
Have you ever had a seizure or been diagnosed with epilepsy?
Do you snore loudly, stop breathing, or gasp during sleep?
Have you recently had major sleep deprivation, psychological stress, fever, alcohol use, or a change in medication?

DIAGNOSIS: NREM sleepwalking (somnambulism), an idiopathic disorder of incomplete arousal from deep non-REM sleep

ALTERNATIVE 1: Confusional arousals, another disorder of incomplete NREM awakening

ALTERNATIVE 2: REM sleep behavior disorder

ALTERNATIVE 3: Sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy
